chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Ayub ibn Nuh, who said:

I wrote to him that our companions had differed regarding us, so some of them said: 'The departure (Nafar) on the last day (13th of Dhul-Hijjah) after midday (Zawal) is superior,' and some of them said: 'Before midday.' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Do you not know that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed Dhuhr and Asr in Mecca, so that could not have been except when they had already departed before midday?'
And whoever wishes to stay in Mina after the departure, let him stay without difficulty.

key_terms.الزَّوَال: Midday (when the sun begins to decline from its zenith)

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred time to depart Mina on the 13th of Dhul-Hijjah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* resolves the juristic dispute regarding the timing of the Mina departure by anchoring the ruling in the Sunnah of the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) actual practice of combining prayers in Mecca, thereby proving the departure occurred before midday. It establishes the principle of *takhayyur* (flexibility), allowing pilgrims to extend their stay in Mina for the full three days if they choose, reflecting the Shia emphasis on following the Prophet’s practical example while accommodating ease for the community.
